phases.text:
📺 Lie Detector. Answer questions. The System knows when you lie. The audience loves when you do.

The audience expects entertainment, not blood.

The lights come up. You can hear the crowd — millions of them, somewhere past the sky.

Two chairs. One scanner. The System knows when you lie — and the audience lives for it.

First question's coming. Your opponent is already sweating.

do.note: You tell the truth. The scanner stays quiet. The audience is disappointed and impressed.
You lie like it's an art form. The scanner buzzes. The audience GASPS with delight.
You say nothing. Silence, televised. The System notes the defiance.

phases.text:
Harder questions now. Personal ones. The scanner hums.

Your opponent just lied badly about something small. The crowd smells blood.

do.note: You commit to the story. The scanner screams. The audience is feral with joy.
You confess — the small thing, the real thing. The scanner goes quiet. The crowd doesn't know what to do with honesty.
You point at the question itself. "Who benefits from asking that?" The System pauses. Interesting.

phases.text:
Final question. The big one. The scanner is hot.

Whatever you say next will be clipped and replayed for years.

do.note: You tell all of it. Every ugly true thing. The scanner is silent. The audience is silent. Then — applause like weather.
You deliver a lie so beautiful the scanner hesitates. The crowd erupts. You win the moment, if not the truth.
You stand and leave. The cameras follow you to the door. The System lets you go — the refusal IS the content.

phases.text:
📺 Grudge Pudding — you and your favorite rival have a grudge.

The System knows. Everyone knows. You must cook a pudding together, on camera. The pudding is a metaphor. The grudge is not.

do.note: Somewhere between the custard and the crust, the grudge runs out of fuel. The pudding is perfect. You split it on camera and the village exhales.
Your half is flawless. Their half is flawless. You do not speak except about temperatures. The pudding wins awards. The grudge continues, televised.
You salt their half on camera, clearly, deliberately. The judges taste it. The galaxy tastes your pettiness. The pudding is ruined and so, briefly, are you.

Recipe: Bow (Level 3). You can make one. Season the wood or it follows the string and dies. Brace it low at first and watch the limbs — they tell you where they want wood removed.
Recipe: Crossbow (Level 3). You can make one. The stock carries the draw so your arms don't have to. Cut the nut from hardwood and test the catch a hundred times before you trust it near your face.
Recipe: Arrow (Level 3). You can make them. Spine matters: too stiff and they fishtail, too soft and they wobble. Match the shaft to the bow and they fly like they mean it.
Recipe: Crossbow bolt (Level 3). You can make them. Keep them short and heavy; the crossbow's power forgives ugly. Five at a time, always — a crossbow with one bolt is a club.
